## LLM Recipe

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

#### [Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36983>)

This study separates data curation that reaches an existing solution sooner from curation that improves attainable target performance, and tests a baseline training-target loss-gap diagnostic. Controlled small-model experiments show why target alignment and training budget should be examined before interpreting a fixed-budget gain as a lasting capability improvement.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.983Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Data Curation, Target Distribution, Training Budgets, Scaling Diagnostics

**Public availability:** 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36983v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Main methods/results and relevant appendices inspected. Five-run SlimPajama experiments at 160M show near-matched-target perplexities 19.71 for Uniform and 19.66 for TANDEM, versus 28.60/26.02 with repeated scarce-domain data; 1.1B tests retain the contrast. Selection separately varies target distributions. Delta is measured halfway through baseline training. Original October 28 cs.LG batch and official Tuesday schedule imply 00:00 UTC announcement. Author code remains pending internal approval.

**Limitations:** The endpoint theorem assumes global population-risk minimization; finite LLM budgets do not verify infinite-budget optimality. Delta compares seen-training and target losses, not distributions, so equal losses can hide mismatch. Selection uses target-aware reference data and unequal retained tokens versus full-pool training. Models stop at 1.1B; no complete end-to-end curation-cost benefit was demonstrated.

### 1.2 Model Architecture &amp; Scaling Laws

#### [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37645>)

MERLIN stores compact first and second moments of each segment’s keys and uses query-dependent alignment means and variances to combine recurrent-memory readouts. Mid-training improves long-context retrieval in two small recurrent backbones, offering a more informative alternative to routing from mean keys alone while retaining an explicit memory-quality trade-off.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.982Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Recurrent Memory, Linear Attention, Moment Routing, Long Context

**Public availability:** 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37645v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Complete 20-page v1 inspected. Uniform 256-token segments and RULER-style augmented mid-training convert Gated DeltaNet-1.3B/Mamba-2-780M to multi-state models. At 16K, LongBench averages reach 21.9/20.6 versus mean-routing 19.3/18.4; RULER averages 62.7/76.2 versus 57.9/71.2. These are benchmark scores, not percentage-point gains from the abstract’s relative percentages. Original October 28 cs.CL new listing and official Tuesday schedule imply 00:00 UTC announcement. No author implementation destination was verified.

**Limitations:** One recorded seed and two backbones at 16K; some individual tasks regress. The state bank grows with segment count, and second-moment storage adds overhead; no measured serving speedup is established. The softmax connection motivates rather than exactly reproduces attention. Main text adds 60M second-stage tokens while appendix summarizes 2B, leaving budget accounting imperfect.

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

#### [EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37062>)

EnergyCal attenuates routed-expert updates using their energy after Muon’s matrix transform, leaving that transform unchanged and adding no persistent optimizer state. Three-initialization tests on one 4B mixture-of-experts model reduce observed loss-spike burden, suggesting a lightweight stability intervention while leaving its causal mechanism and generality unresolved.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.982Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Muon, Mixture of Experts, Training Stability, Update Scaling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37062v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Methods, cohorts and diagnostic appendices inspected. With plain Muon at matched nominal learning rate and decay, thresholded spike burden falls 94.99%/96.97% for exponents 0.5/1 across three paired initializations. Runs use 1.31B tokens and eight H100s. The separate MuonH comparison changes learning rate and loses 1.62% throughput. Original October 28 cs.LG new listing and official Tuesday schedule imply 00:00 UTC announcement. No available author implementation was verified.

**Limitations:** All runs finish; burden is not failure probability. A missing routed-only uniform-scaling control leaves energy-specific benefit unresolved. Local interventions fail to rescue two spikes. Endpoint quality gains with plain Muon are small, its timing is unmeasured, and differing validation banks prohibit cross-cohort ranking. One short-budget architecture cannot establish general optimizer superiority.

### 2.2 Tool Use &amp; Environment Interaction

#### [Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37461>)

This full-paper study evaluates an existing library that derives finite-state tool protocols from agent classes, exposes only currently legal tools and blocks illegal calls before execution. Its pressured airline experiments show why authorization should be checked separately from task success, while making the limits of keyword-based confirmation explicit.

ClaimNov extracts typed research claims, compares them with evidence from a supplied prior-work pool and gives a final judge the resulting claim-level profile. This helps a scientific agent reject repackaged work while preserving proposals that combine established components with new contributions.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

#### [TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37230>)

TAO jointly admits and places agent sessions using decayed node-specific cache credit, predicted tool-return readiness and token footprint. A snapshot dynamic program coordinates competing sessions, while live revalidation keeps stale plans within current admission limits; this can reduce waiting and recover useful cache locality.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.371Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agentic Serving, Joint Placement, Cache Locality, Tool Readiness

With DeepSeek-V4 Flash on two four-H100 nodes, SWE-Lite at 64 workers reduces mean task latency 253.228→185.410 seconds and raises aggregate decode 1561.307→2021.523 tokens/s versus the best respective baseline. Original October 28 cs.DC listing and Tuesday 20:00 Eastern schedule imply October 28 00:00 UTC announcement; October 27 is the submission date. No author artifact destination was verified.

**Limitations:** Natural-live runs generate differing trajectories; repeated-run uncertainty and equal task success are not established. Some settings regress, including mixed AutomationBench at 128 workers. Optimality covers a quantized snapshot surrogate, not global online latency; fallback and failed-search costs are excluded from the reported scheduler-work fraction. CPU tools retain separate resource budgets.

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36520>)

This method approximately folds static per-key attention biases into existing key dimensions using a context-fitted direction, then refits values. The resulting compacted cache uses ordinary attention kernels and an unchanged query path, making biased compaction easier to serve without adding a head coordinate.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.494Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** KV Compaction, Attention Bias, Serving Compatibility, Query Drift

**Public availability:** 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36520v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. All 30 pages, including serving and budget ablations, inspected. Unmodified vLLM matches Hugging Face answer letters on 51 Qwen3-4 B questions and complete greedy outputs on 180/200 Qwen3-14 B LongBench samples from the same folded cache. These test integration, not preservation of full-cache quality. Original October 28 cs.LG listing plus Tuesday 20:00 Eastern schedule imply October 28 00:00 UTC announcement; receipt is October 27. No author implementation destination was verified.

**Limitations:** Exactness requires each query’s fitted projection to equal 1; drift and value refitting can cause losses. Small QA comparisons lack equivalence power; a Llama/LongHealth setting loses 4.5 percentage points to biased Attention Matching. Advantages over dropping bias depend on per-head budgets. Larger-model capacity/peak-decode tests use random weights and exclude fitting cost; they establish neither end-to-end speed nor answer quality.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [PipeLink: new contract interfaces and GEMM–SwiGLU composition evaluation](<https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/PipeLink>)

PipeLink packages separately compiled GPU components with resource and synchronization contracts, then checks, places and links them into a fused kernel. Its new GEMM–SwiGLU study shows how CUDA and TileLang consumers can reuse architecture-specific producers without their source, approaching equivalent single-compilation performance.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:02:23.371Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** GPU Component Linking, Contract Checking, Operator Fusion, CUDA and TileLang

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37200v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/PipeLink>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and pinned code inspected. The new Qwen3-32 B MLP study uses B300, H200 and RTX 5090; at M=16,384 its B300 composition reaches 1.20× cuBLAS plus compiled activation, but only 0.98–0.99× hand fusion. Across 51 tested configurations, linked performance stays within 0.2% of equivalent single-unit controls.

**Limitations:** Contracts are checked against declarations, not opaque component bodies; sanitizers and numerical tests remain necessary. Packages target one architecture/toolkit, and transfers do not synthesize arithmetic or collectives. Published reports omit raw timing receipts and executable bundles; no experiments were reproduced.
